name: canli-backtest-mcp

tools.name: list_factors
tools.description: The point-in-time factors pit_factor builds from SEC filings, and what each measures.

tools.name: pit_factor
tools.description: Build a factor from SEC filings for a list of tickers, monthly from start to end, using only what had been filed by each date (restatements invisible until filed). Writes a signal CSV for backtest_signal. Values are what companies reported to the SEC in XBRL, as filed by each date; a company that files late, files outside XBRL or changes its tags can be missing.

factor.description: One of roa, gross_margin, operating_margin, revenue_growth, asset_growth, accruals, or level:<measure> (revenue, net_income, assets, ...).

tickers.description: Tickers (or CIKs) to compute it for.

out_file.description: Where to write the signal CSV; default a new temporary file.

tools.name: backtest_signal
tools.description: Backtest a signal against your prices: rank, long and short quantiles, rebalance, trading only on what was known lag_days earlier, costs on actual trades. Pass ledger to judge the best of a search against all of it. A backtest measures one path of history under these costs; it does not establish that the signal will keep working.

prices_file.description: CSV: a date column (YYYY-MM-DD) and one column of closing prices per ticker.

signal_file.description: CSV in the same shape; each row dated when its values became known (pit_factor writes this).

rebalance.description: Default monthly; or every N trading days.

lag_days.description: Trading days between a signal becoming known and trading on it. Default 1, the minimum.

side.description: Default long_short: long the top quantile, short the bottom.

quantile.description: Fraction of ranked names in each leg. Default 0.2.

cost_bps.description: Cost per unit traded, in basis points. Default 10.

min_names.description: Skip a rebalance with fewer ranked names. Default 5.

ledger.description: Record this run in a search ledger (created if new) and judge it against every run recorded there.

label.description: The variant's name in the ledger. Default: the settings.

instructions: Backtests that refuse lookahead. Build a point-in-time factor from SEC filings with pit_factor (or bring your own signal CSV, each row dated when it was known), then run backtest_signal against your own prices CSV. Pass the same ledger name to every backtest_signal call in one search: the reply judges the best variant against all of them.
